name: swipe-row

frames.best_why: The first row is fully open, showing the red Delete action with its bin icon next to the message.

tagline: Mail rows slide aside under a finger to uncover a red Delete button.
summary: A rounded message row that drags sideways with resistance and snaps open to reveal coloured action buttons. Pull far enough and the primary action takes over, then the row collapses away.
appearance: Four dark rounded rows stacked in a column, each holding a circular initials badge, sender name, subject and timestamp. Swiping a row exposes a solid red panel on the right with a white bin icon and the word Delete.
behaviour: Dragging a row sideways moves it with rubber-band give; past halfway it snaps open to show the action panel. A fast flick opens or closes it, and a long pull commits the delete and collapses the row.
demo_content: Four fake inbox rows: Maya Chen, Daniel Okafor, Priya Raman and Lucas Martin with subjects and times.
search_phrases: drag a row to reveal delete
use_when: A touch list needs quick per-item actions without opening a detail screen or adding visible buttons.
avoid_when: Sideways drags compete with browser back gestures and are awkward with a mouse; it needs pointer events.
customise: Actions array, action and drawer colours, row height, radius, action width, swipe direction, resistance and commit threshold are props; the row's own content is passed as children.
weight_why: One motion value per row plus a spring on release; nothing runs until a row is touched.

a11y.note: Keyboard users get a small toggle button to open the row and delete; the drag itself is pointer-only and reduced motion is not checked.

polish_why: Tight, believable iOS-style motion and a clear red action; timestamps are very low contrast.
title: Swipe Row
